title: 一件家具从设计到上架，怎样协调各团队？
topic: 跨设计、生产、物流与零售团队推进产品

source.title: The story about the IKEA value chain
source.section: The story about the IKEA value chain
source.type: 宜家官方业务流程与价值链介绍
source.context: 宜家 宜家官方业务流程与价值链介绍。
paragraphs: If you could boil IKEA into a broth, you’d end up with 10 words at the bottom of the pan. “To create a better everyday life for the many people.” That’s our vision, and we try to fulfil it through a wide range of well-designed, functional home furnishing products at prices so low that as many people as possible can afford them.

The IKEA value chain works around the clock, across the planet. That’s why finding clever ways for products and components to get from one end of the value chain to our customers’ home is so important.

Democratic Design helps us create products with the almost impossible combination of form, function, quality, sustainability, and a low price. All five are important, and how we balance them depends on the job that the product has in our range. It may sound strange, but the first thing we design is the price tag. Because ultimately, the low price serves as the welcome committee of IKEA. To arrive at a low price, we strive for low costs in everything we do.
Democratic design only works when we work together. Designers, engineers, product developers, sourcing specialist, well, everyone.
With that scale comes the opportunity to work with many people, partners and suppliers across the IKEA value chain.

Our suppliers are part of the gang, too. In many cases they become long-term partners, not only supplying IKEA with products, but also new ideas and knowledge. It’s a genuine partnership and quite often the product design and production method are perfected on the factory floor. Sometimes it even starts there! What do we already have and can we use that in a new way?
translations: 如果把宜家熬成一锅浓汤，最后沉淀下来的会是十个词：“为大众创造更美好的日常生活。”这是宜家的愿景。宜家通过种类丰富、设计良好、功能实用且价格低到尽可能让更多人买得起的家居产品来实现这一愿景。
宜家的价值链全天候、跨地域运转。因此，找到巧妙的方法，让产品和零部件从价值链的一端抵达顾客家中非常重要。
“民主设计”帮助宜家把造型、功能、质量、可持续性和低价这几乎不可能兼顾的要素结合起来。五项都重要，如何平衡取决于产品在产品系列中的作用。听起来或许奇怪，但我们最先设计的是价格标签，因为低价最终能让更多人走进宜家。为了实现低价，我们努力降低各个环节的成本。
民主设计只有在大家共同协作时才行得通，包括设计师、工程师、产品开发人员、采购专员，实际上每个人都要参与。
这样的规模也带来机会，让团队能与宜家价值链中的许多人、合作伙伴和供应商一起工作。
供应商也是团队的一部分。很多供应商后来成为长期伙伴，不仅向宜家提供产品，也带来新的想法和知识。这是真正的合作关系；产品设计和生产方式往往会在工厂车间得到完善，有时创意也是从那里开始的。我们已有的资源是什么？能否用新的方式加以利用？
fullTextParagraphs: This is a story about the integrated IKEA value chain. But first, what’s a value chain and what does it mean when we say that it’s integrated? Let’s find out!

If you could boil IKEA into a broth, you’d end up with 10 words at the bottom of the pan. “To create a better everyday life for the many people.” That’s our vision, and we try to fulfil it through a wide range of well-designed, functional home furnishing products at prices so low that as many people as possible can afford them.

One of the cornerstones of IKEA is a never-ending curiosity. Since the 70’s, we’ve made thousands of home visits to figure out how people live. It would’ve been more convenient to sit in a warm office in Älmhult and guess, but that’s not us. So, we knock on doors, chat to people, look through cabinets, drawers, and boxes – always looking for a better understanding of what life at home really looks like. Then we use that knowledge to figure out products that make a difference.

The IKEA value chain works around the clock, across the planet. That’s why finding clever ways for products and components to get from one end of the value chain to our customers’ home is so important.

Democratic Design helps us create products with the almost impossible combination of form, function, quality, sustainability, and a low price. All five are important, and how we balance them depends on the job that the product has in our range. It may sound strange, but the first thing we design is the price tag. Because ultimately, the low price serves as the welcome committee of IKEA. To arrive at a low price, we strive for low costs in everything we do.
Democratic design only works when we work together. Designers, engineers, product developers, sourcing specialist, well, everyone.
With that scale comes the opportunity to work with many people, partners and suppliers across the IKEA value chain.

Materials used in IKEA products account for the largest share of the IKEA climate footprint. That is why we focus on developing and exploring new materials, while making informed material choices throughout the design process.

We work to integrate environmental and social considerations across our business, from product development and sourcing to production and retail. We focus on increasing the use of renewable and recycled materials in our products and on reducing greenhouse gas emissions across the IKEA value chain.

Our suppliers are part of the gang, too. In many cases they become long-term partners, not only supplying IKEA with products, but also new ideas and knowledge. It’s a genuine partnership and quite often the product design and production method are perfected on the factory floor. Sometimes it even starts there! What do we already have and can we use that in a new way?

We have the ambition to influence every little part in our value chain to the better. We believe that taking responsibility is a privilege. IWAY, which is the IKEA supplier code of conduct, help us to make sure that we practice what we preach. IWAY is a set of very clear rules that regulates every little thing from environmental, social and working conditions to animal welfare. It’s about doing the right thing – together.

Logistics and efficient transportation have always played an important role at IKEA. The flatpack, that first saw the light of day in 1952, was the start of the modern, rebellious IKEA. Funnily enough, the flatpack still says a lot about who we are. We genuinely dislike wasting resources by transporting air, which is why efficient packaging is part of our design process, and not an afterthought.
It costs less because you assemble it yourself, it’s well-protected and it’s been transported in the most efficient way possible.

Shopping at IKEA used to be synonymous with going to a big blue box on the outskirts of town. Today, the blue box is just one of many places where our customers meet us. Our ambition is to always be close to where people find it convenient to meet us.

In the mid 80’s, our founder Ingvar Kamprad decided that IKEA should be operated in a franchise system. IKEA is one brand, but if you look under the hood, you’ll find many different companies with different owners, working together in the integrated value chain. We are more than 215.000 co-workers, sharing the same vision, culture and values. Together with our partners, we connect millions of people daily.
Speaking of togetherness, if we had a superpower, it would probably be that we do things together. We grow, fail and learn together. That is our value chain, and why we believe it is quite unique.

scenario.title: 模拟新品上市协同：家具样品已定，门店日期待确认
english: The design team has approved a new flat-pack desk.
The factory needs the final material list, logistics needs a delivery window, and retail needs a shelf date.
You need to line up the owners and propose the next check-in.
chinese: 设计团队已批准一款新平板包装书桌。
工厂需要最终材料清单，物流需要到货时间窗，零售团队需要上架日期。
你要确认各项负责人，并提出下一次同步时间。

firstAttempt.prompt: 模拟新品协同：设计团队已批准一款平板包装书桌；工厂待确认最终材料清单，物流待确认到货时间窗，零售团队待确认上架日期。请用英语确认各团队的待办，并提出下一次同步时间。
firstAttempt.sample: Before we confirm the launch date, we need to confirm the final material list and production date with the factory, the delivery window with logistics, and the shelf date with retail. Could we hold a cross-functional review on Thursday to confirm an owner for each item?
firstAttempt.rationale: 说明工厂、物流和零售各自要确认的事项，再约定评审时间和负责人。

taskPhrases.collocation: confirm a detail with a team
taskPhrases.example: We need to confirm the production date with the factory.
taskPhrases.translation: 我们需要和工厂确认生产日期。

taskPhrases.example: Before we confirm the launch date, we need a delivery window.
taskPhrases.translation: 确定上架日期前，我们需要先拿到到货时间窗。

taskPhrases.word: Could we hold a review on…?
taskPhrases.meaning: 我们能否在……安排一次评审会？
taskPhrases.example: Could we hold a cross-functional review on Thursday?
taskPhrases.translation: 我们能否在周四安排一次跨部门评审会？

words.example: We need input from teams across the value chain.
words.translation: 我们需要价值链各环节团队提供意见。
words.note: 从产品开发到交付顾客的各个环节。

words.example: We’ll confirm the material lead time with the supplier.
words.translation: 我们会和供应商确认材料交期。
words.note: 提供产品、材料或服务的合作方。

words.example: We need to balance cost, quality, and delivery timing.
words.translation: 我们需要兼顾成本、质量和交付时间。
words.note: 常用于说明多个目标之间的取舍。

structure.original: Democratic design only works when we work together.
analysis: only works when 表示只有满足某个条件，某方法才行得通。
when 后接完整句子，说明共同协作是前提。
structure.transfer: The launch plan only works when product, operations, and retail agree on the dates.

rewrite.bad: The factory, logistics, and retail teams need to coordinate.
rewrite.good: Before we confirm the launch date, we need to confirm the final material list and production date with the factory, the delivery window with logistics, and the shelf date with retail. Could we hold a cross-functional review on Thursday to confirm an owner for each item?
rewrite.translation: 确定上市日期前，我们需要和工厂确认最终材料清单和生产日期、和物流团队确认到货时间窗、和零售团队确认上架日期。我们能否在周四开一次跨部门评审，确定每项任务的负责人？
rewrite.pattern: Before we confirm [date], we need [input] from [team]. Could we review [dependencies] on [date] and assign owners?

cloze.prompt: We need to confirm the production date ______ the factory.
cloze.why: confirm something with a team 表示与团队核实事项。

cloze.prompt: Before we confirm the launch date, we need a delivery ______.
cloze.why: delivery window 指可交付的时间范围。

cloze.prompt: Could we hold a cross-functional ______ on Thursday?
cloze.why: review 在这里指共同检查进度和待办。

dictation.text: The value chain works across the planet.
dictation.why: 听清 value chain 和 across the planet，说明协作跨地域展开。

dictation.text: Democratic design only works when we work together.
dictation.why: 注意 only works when 表达的条件关系。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们需要和工厂确认生产日期。
translationPractice.answer: We need to confirm the production date with the factory.
translationPractice.why: 先明确需要哪些团队提供信息。

translationPractice.prompt: 确定上架日期前，我们需要先拿到到货时间窗。
translationPractice.answer: Before we confirm the launch date, we need a delivery window.
translationPractice.why: 把生产、交付和上架日期作为相互依赖的事项来确认。

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否在周四安排一次跨部门评审会？
translationPractice.answer: Could we hold a cross-functional review on Thursday?
translationPractice.why: 约定时间，让相关团队一起确认依赖和负责人。

choice.prompt: 工厂交期可能晚一周，门店已经排好上架活动。你该怎样同步？
options: The factory is late, so retail should change its plan.
The factory delivery may move by a week. Could we confirm the revised date with logistics and retail today, then agree on an updated shelf date?
The launch will probably be delayed.
choice.why: 说明变化、拉齐受影响团队，并把日期确认到位。

output.prompt: 一批新产品需要工厂、仓库和客服团队共同准备。请说明各方待确认事项，并约定下一次同步。
output.sample: Before we confirm the launch, the factory needs to send the final product list, the warehouse needs to confirm the intake date, and customer support needs to review the product details. Could we meet on Wednesday to check these dependencies and assign an owner to each item?
check: 列出至少两项跨团队依赖
说明由谁确认哪些信息
提出明确的下一次同步安排
